handbookNote: North Carolina DMV Motorcyclists' Handbook, Thirteenth Edition, September 2007 (content courtesy of the Motorcycle Safety Foundation) -- price matches this project's established Motorcycle tier ($7.99), not a placeholder. This is the current official manual: the direct PDF link published on ncdot.gov/dmv/license-id/driver-licenses/new-drivers/Documents/motorcyclist-handbook.pdf (linked from the official handbooks page) is this same Thirteenth Edition, so no live re-fetch was needed. EXAM MECHANICS PARTIALLY HEDGED: NC's motorcycle knowledge test is NOT broadly waived -- confirmed via ncdot.gov/dmv/license-id/driver-licenses/motorcycle (requires 'Pass a motorcycle knowledge test') and the handbook itself (p.5, 'Licensing and Registration'), which states the knowledge test is waived only on a license renewal, and that completing the skills test is separate from the knowledge test; the written knowledge test remains required for all standard first-time/endorsement applicants. However, neither ncdot.gov's motorcycle licensing page nor the handbook itself publishes an exact item count or passing percentage for the knowledge test anywhere checked this session. Third-party test-prep sites (driving-tests.org, zutobi.com, epermittest.com, dmv-permit-test.com and others) most consistently report a 25-question test with 20 correct (80%) required to pass, though at least one source cites a conflicting 37-question/78% format; NEITHER figure is officially confirmed by NCDMV and MUST be flagged as an unconfirmed stand-in in the EXAM_CONFIGS code comment at wiring time, same convention as other hedged tracks (e.g. pa_motorcycle, tx_motorcycle).
